concepts.name: Market Structure
concepts.summary: Swing highs/lows, Break of Structure (BOS), Market Structure Shift (MSS). Use the higher timeframe to frame directional context; define the swing and close rule before testing.

concepts.name: Liquidity
concepts.summary: Buy-side and sell-side liquidity; EQH/EQL; PDH/PDL; PWH/PWL; session highs/lows; internal and external range liquidity. A sweep is not an entry by itself.

concepts.name: Displacement
concepts.summary: A fast directional move with relatively large candle bodies that breaks a meaningful swing and may leave an imbalance. Define objective criteria for a backtest.

concepts.name: Fair Value Gap (FVG)
concepts.summary: Three-candle imbalance: bullish when candle 3 low is above candle 1 high; bearish when candle 3 high is below candle 1 low. CE is the midpoint. An FVG is a zone, not a guaranteed signal.

concepts.name: IFVG & BPR
concepts.summary: IFVG: a gap whose polarity changes after a qualifying body close through its far edge. BPR: overlap of bullish and bearish FVGs. Define mitigation by wick or close.

concepts.name: Order Block & Breaker
concepts.summary: OB: last opposing candle/zone before a displacement move. Breaker: failed OB whose polarity reverses. Require the displacement and define body-vs-wick boundaries.

concepts.name: Unicorn & Mitigation
concepts.summary: Unicorn is the overlap of a breaker block and FVG in the described model. Mitigation block is treated as a distinct zone concept; exact rules vary across practitioners.

concepts.name: Premium / Discount
concepts.summary: Choose a structural dealing range, mark equilibrium at 50%; above = premium, below = discount. Do not redraw the range after seeing the outcome.

concepts.name: OTE
concepts.summary: The PDF describes the 62–79% retracement band, with 70.5% as a midpoint convention. Pair it with a real impulse leg, key level and defined invalidation.

concepts.name: Time Anchors
concepts.summary: Midnight Open, 08:30 ET data reference, 09:30 ET cash open, NDOG/NWOG. A gap across the exchange maintenance break is not automatically an FVG.

concepts.name: AMD / Power of Three
concepts.summary: Accumulation, Manipulation and Distribution as a daily narrative. Use as a hypothesis, not proof that an early move must reverse.

concepts.name: Judas Swing
concepts.summary: A session-associated false push through a marked level followed by a move in the opposite direction. Requires a pre-existing directional hypothesis and confirmation.

concepts.name: IPDA 20/40/60
concepts.summary: The playbook frames 20-, 40- and 60-trading-day highs/lows as reference liquidity ranges. Treat “algorithm” language as a model, not an established mechanism.

concepts.name: SMT Divergence
concepts.summary: Related markets make non-confirming highs/lows around a meaningful level. Match session, swing timing and expiry; use as a filter, not a standalone trigger.

concepts.name: Weekly Profiles
concepts.summary: Tuesday/Wednesday weekly-high/low profiles and midweek reversal tendencies. Treat as tendencies to record and test, never fixed weekday rules.

concepts.name: PD Arrays
concepts.summary: Umbrella term for reference zones such as old highs/lows, FVGs, order blocks, breakers, liquidity voids and rejection blocks. Premium/discount is the range framework; PD Arrays are the reference levels within it.

concepts.name: Volume Imbalance
concepts.summary: A price gap between two consecutive candle bodies while their wicks overlap. It is distinct from the three-candle FVG definition.

concepts.name: First Presented FVG (FPFVG)
concepts.summary: The session’s first FVG that meets a trader-defined qualification rule. The PDF labels its perceived quality as a community convention, not a proven edge.

concepts.name: CBDR & Flout
concepts.summary: Central Bank Dealers Range (typically 14:00–20:00 ET in the PDF) and the extended Flout range (sources differ on the start). Record candle-body vs full-range measurement rules.

concepts.name: Standard-Deviation Projections
concepts.summary: The PDF uses the anchor range height as a “1 SD” unit and projects multiples such as ±1, ±2 and ±2.5. This is not statistical standard deviation; it is a range projection convention.

concepts.name: Weekly Profiles
concepts.summary: Tuesday/Wednesday weekly-high or weekly-low profiles and midweek reversal tendencies. They describe possible timing patterns, not deterministic calendar effects.

models.name: Liquidity Sweep + MSS
models.context: At a meaningful HTF/session level, price wicks through a visible liquidity pool and closes back inside; wait for displacement and MSS.
models.entry: After the shift, use a defined FVG/OB pullback.
models.invalidation: No MSS/displacement or no valid pullback = no setup.

models.name: Silver Bullet
models.context: Three one-hour New York windows in the playbook: 03:00–04:00, 10:00–11:00 and 14:00–15:00 ET.
models.entry: Only use an FVG formed inside the chosen window after context and trigger conditions.
models.stop: Beyond manipulation swing / model-defined far edge.
models.invalidation: No qualifying FVG inside the window = no trade.

models.name: ICT 2022 Model
models.context: Raid a relevant liquidity pool, then displacement/MSS with an imbalance. The PDF uses 15M–1H for pools and 1M–5M execution.
models.invalidation: Any required chain element missing = setup invalid.

models.name: Judas + MSS
models.context: Session opening fake push through a marked level in the context of a pre-defined HTF bias.
models.entry: Wait for opposite displacement and an FVG/OB pullback.
models.target: Opposite liquidity; SD levels only as secondary references.
models.invalidation: No HTF bias or no reversal confirmation = no trade.

models.name: Unicorn
models.context: Breaker block and FVG overlap after a sweep and displacement/shift.
models.entry: The overlap zone, using explicitly defined boundaries.
models.invalidation: No overlap = ordinary breaker/FVG, not Unicorn.

models.name: FVG Continuation
models.context: A directional impulse produces a qualifying FVG with HTF/session alignment.
models.entry: Pullback into FVG, often CE midpoint.
models.stop: Beyond the far edge or structural invalidation.
models.invalidation: Body close through the gap invalidates the idea per the chosen rule.

models.name: IFVG
models.context: Price closes through the far edge of an FVG, changing its role; a retest may be studied as a setup.
models.entry: Retest of the inverted FVG after confirmation.
models.invalidation: The PDF labels this popular but without robust public stats.

models.name: FVG + OTE
models.context: An impulsive leg and FVG overlap with the 62–79% retracement band.
models.entry: FVG/OB inside the pre-defined OTE zone.
models.stop: Beyond the swing anchor / setup invalidation.
models.invalidation: Do not use Fibonacci on a non-impulsive or redefined leg.

sessions.name: Asian Range
sessions.purpose: Mark overnight range extremes / accumulation reference.

sessions.name: Midnight Open
sessions.purpose: Daily reference price; not a trade window.
sessions.ist: ET converted using the current NY offset.

sessions.name: London Killzone
sessions.purpose: London session sweep, Judas and currency/metals setups.

sessions.name: NY AM Index / Metals
sessions.purpose: Primary index and metals preparation/execution window.

sessions.name: NY Lunch — Caution
sessions.purpose: The PDF marks this as an avoid window across the playbook.

sessions.name: PM Silver Bullet
sessions.purpose: One-hour FVG model window; FOMC often overlaps this period.

sessions.name: CME Maintenance Break
sessions.purpose: PDF reference for most CME Globex futures; confirm product and holiday schedules.
